tetsu-tf6-warriors.name: Warriors and Junk (Arrest)
tetsu-tf6-warriors.blurb: Trudge's "Emergency arrest!" deck in Tag Force 6: Junk Synchron, Dasher, Torapart and Kuraz with Goyo Guardian and the Junk Synchro and X-Saber line. It is a playable version with printed cards, not a deck shown in the anime.
tetsu-tf6-warriors.basis: Trudge's "Emergency arrest!" list in Tag Force 6, as the wiki records it; every card is from that list.

tetsu-transer-chasing.name: Security Chase
tetsu-transer-chasing.blurb: Trudge's "Chasing Security" deck in Duel Transer: Blocker, Gatekeeper, Cyber Commander and Pursuit Chaser with Security Orb, No Entry!! and Broken Blocker. It is a playable version with printed cards, not a deck shown in the anime.
tetsu-transer-chasing.basis: Trudge's "Chasing Security" list in Duel Transer, as the wiki records it; every card is from that list.

tetsu-transer-goyo.name: Goyo Security
tetsu-transer-goyo.blurb: Officer Trudge's deck: Stygian Street Patrol and Stygian Security, Handcuffs Dragon, Goyo Guardian and Stygian Sergeants, with No Entry!! and Security Orb.
tetsu-transer-goyo.basis: Thematic deck: the anime shows no deck for this character. It is built from the list he uses in the video game (Duel Transer) and the cards that define him.

yusei-bond-morning-star.name: Bond of Morning Star
yusei-bond-morning-star.blurb: Yusei's deck in Duel Transer: Junk Synchron and Quickdraw Synchron, Tuning x3, Miracle Synchro Fusion and an Extra Deck full of Warriors alongside Stardust Dragon and Majestic Star Dragon.

yusei-dark-signer-junk.name: Junk Synchron and Stardust Dragon
yusei-dark-signer-junk.blurb: Yusei's deck in the Dark Signers saga: Junk Synchron, the support Synchrons and Junk Warrior, Road Warrior and Stardust Dragon to finish. A fast-Synchro deck with protection traps.

yusei-pre-wrgp-junk.name: Junk Warrior and Max Warrior
yusei-pre-wrgp-junk.blurb: Yusei's deck before the World Racing Grand Prix: a tower of Synchrons (Bri, Drill, Changer, Quickdraw) and Tuner tricks to bring out Junk Warrior, Armory Arm and Stardust Dragon.

yusei-vjump-synchron.name: V-Jump Synchrons
yusei-vjump-synchron.blurb: Yusei's deck published in V-Jump magazine: the whole Synchron family (Junk, Quickdraw, Explorer), Tuningware and Tuning to Synchro into Junk Warrior, Nitro Warrior and Stardust Dragon. It is a playable version with printed cards, not a deck shown in the anime.
yusei-vjump-synchron.basis: Yusei's list from V-Jump magazine as the wiki records it (Synchron, Tuningware, Tuning, De-Synchro and the Synchro Warriors). No card is filler: all are from that list.

alito-battlin-boxer.name: Battlin' Boxer
alito-battlin-boxer.blurb: Alito's deck: Battlin' Boxers that climb to Number 105 and Number C105: Battlin' Boxer Comet Cestus. Their anime-only spells and traps are swapped for printed Xyz and Boxer support.

astral-na-wcq-2014.name: Number 39 (WCQ 2014)
astral-na-wcq-2014.blurb: Astral's deck in the duels of the 2014 North American qualifier: Gagaga with Number 39: Utopia and Number 11: Big Eye.

bronk-gearspring-thematic.name: Bronk's Gearspring
bronk-gearspring-thematic.blurb: Bronk, Yuma's skater friend, plays a machine deck: Tin Goldfish, Aye-Iron, Gearspring Spirit and UFO Turtle, with Iron Call and Iron Draw, to climb to Tin Archduke and Number 39: Utopia.
bronk-gearspring-thematic.basis: Base: Bronk's deck from the wiki (his duels in episodes 1, 11 and 20): four machine monsters, Tin Archduke, Number 39: Utopia, Iron Call, Iron Draw, Monster Reborn and Rush Recklessly. Spells and traps that only exist in the anime are swapped for cards real lists play, and the rest is filled by the monsters and spells those lists use. It is a thematic deck, not one seen on screen.

girag-pressure-point-thematic.name: Pressure Point Hands
girag-pressure-point-thematic.blurb: Girag fights with his deck of Hands: The Judgement Hand, Fire Hand, Ice Hand, Magic Hand and Prominence Hand, which climb to Number 58: Burner Visor, Number 106: Giant Hand and Number C106: Giant Red Hand.
girag-pressure-point-thematic.basis: Base: Girag's Pressure Point Deck from the wiki (his duel against Alito, episodes 132 and 133): the five Hands, the three Xyz, Reload and the two Rank-Up-Magic. Spells and traps that only exist in the anime are swapped for cards real lists play, and the rest is filled by the monsters and spells those lists use. It is a thematic deck, not one seen on screen.

kite-duelist-pack-photon.name: Photon (Kite Duelist Pack)
kite-duelist-pack-photon.blurb: The promotional list of Kaito's Duelist Pack: Photon and Galaxy with Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon, Neo Galaxy-Eyes and Number 39: Utopia in the Extra Deck.

kite-photon-galaxy-stream.name: Photon Galaxy Stream
kite-photon-galaxy-stream.blurb: V Jump list of Kaito's Photon and Galaxy line: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon, Galaxy Knight, Galaxy Wizard and Galaxy Expedition.

kite-v-jump-deck-profile.name: Kaito's Deck Profile
kite-v-jump-deck-profile.blurb: Kaito's deck profile in V Jump: Photon Cerberus, Photon Caesar and Twin Photon Lizard with Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon as the ace.

kite-v-jump-holy-overed-galaxy.name: Photon Hieratic
kite-v-jump-holy-overed-galaxy.blurb: The V Jump version that mixes the Photons with the Hieratic dragons and their Hieratic Dragon King of Atum, plus Starliege Paladynamo and Constellar for Rank 4.

mizar-thematic.name: Tachyon Dragons
mizar-thematic.blurb: Mizar builds everything around Number 107: Galaxy-Eyes Tachyon Dragon: dragons that Summon themselves or change their Level to 8 to reach Rank 8, and a Galaxy Stealth Dragon to finish.
mizar-thematic.basis: Base: the "Tachyon Dragon" deck the wiki attributes to Mizar (Radius, Heliosphere, Parsec, Schwarzschild Limit, Number 107 and C107). Spells and traps that only exist in the anime are swapped for printed Tachyon/Galaxy-Eyes cards, and the rest is filled by what the real Galaxy Tachyon deck plays. It is a thematic deck, not one seen on screen.

quinton-space-thematic.name: Space Deck
quinton-space-thematic.blurb: Quinton plays a space deck: Deep-Space Cruiser IX, Planet Pathfinder and Solar Wind Jammer to reach Number 9: Dyson Sphere and Number C9: Chaos Dyson Sphere, with Gravity Blaster and Rank-Up-Magic Argent Chaos Force.
quinton-space-thematic.basis: Base: Quinton's Space Deck from the wiki (his duels in episodes 51 to 56 and 116 to 128): three space monsters, the two Dyson Spheres, Gravity Blaster, Tannhauser Gate, Space Gate, Blasting the Ruins and Rank-Up-Magic Argent Chaos Force. Spells and traps that only exist in the anime are swapped for cards real lists play, and the rest is filled by the monsters and spells those lists use. It is a thematic deck, not one seen on screen.

rio-ice-winged-beast-thematic.name: Ice Winged Beasts
rio-ice-winged-beast-thematic.blurb: Rio builds her deck with ice Winged Beasts (Blizzard Falcon, Blizzard Thunderbird, Aurora Wing, Guard Penguin) and climbs to Ice Beast Zerofyne, Ice Princess Zereort and Number 103: Ragnazero. Diamond Dust and Mirror Force protect her.
rio-ice-winged-beast-thematic.basis: Base: the Ice Winged Beast deck the wiki attributes to Rio (plus Marin's Ragnazero): four Winged Beasts, four Xyz, Monster Reborn, Rank-Up-Magic - The Seventh One, Diamond Dust and Mirror Force (the latter seen in an episode 91 flashback). Spells and traps that only exist in the anime are swapped for cards real lists play, and the rest is filled by the monsters and spells those lists use. It is a thematic deck, not one seen on screen.

shark-barian-invasion-shark-fortress.name: Barian Invasion Sharks
shark-barian-invasion-shark-fortress.blurb: The deck of the Barian Invasion arc: the whole Shark family (Hammer, Spear, Panther, Eagle, Double Fin) with Starfish and the Xyz Shark Caesar, Shark Fortress and Shark Drake Veiss. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Xyz support and traps of the same era.

shark-pre-wdc-aero-shark.name: Aero Shark and Leviathan
shark-pre-wdc-aero-shark.blurb: The deck of the first arc, the duel against Yuma: small fish (Shark Stickers, Needle Sunfish, Skull Kraken, Shocktopus) that reach Rank 3 (Aero Shark, Black Ray Lancer) and Number 17: Leviathan Dragon. Anime-only cards are swapped for support from real Shark lists.

shark-v-jump-full-armored-shark.name: Full Armored Shark
shark-v-jump-full-armored-shark.blurb: V Jump list of Shark's deck: Double Shark, Hammer Shark and Mermail Abysspike that reach Black Ray Lancer and Full Armored Black Ray Lancer.

shark-v-jump-waterfall-deity.name: Fury of the Waterfall Deity
shark-v-jump-waterfall-deity.blurb: V Jump list of Shark's sharks: Depth Shark, Saber Shark and Silent Angler, with Number 32: Shark Drake and Number C32: Shark Drake Veiss.

vector-umbral-horror.name: Umbral Horror
vector-umbral-horror.blurb: Vector's deck with the Umbral Horrors and the Barian Number Cs. Many of his traps are anime-only, so they are replaced with printed Umbral Horror and Barian cards.

vetrix-heraldic-beast.name: Heraldic Beast
vetrix-heraldic-beast.blurb: Vetrix's deck: Heraldic Beasts that make Psychic Xyz (Number 8: Heraldic King Genom-Heritage, Number 69: Heraldry Crest). Anime-only Heraldry cards are replaced with printed Heraldic support.

yuma-mythyrian-numbers-war.name: Utopia Ray Victory
yuma-mythyrian-numbers-war.blurb: The deck of the fifth season: Gagaga, Toy Knight and the Utopias (Roots, Ray, Ray Victory) with Rank-Up-Magic Numeron Force. Anime-only traps and spells are replaced with printed Xyz cards of the same role.

yuma-numbers-guide-2-zw.name: Gagaga and ZW
yuma-numbers-guide-2-zw.blurb: The deck from the Numbers 2 guide: Gagaga with the ZW weapons (Unicorn Spear, Tornado Bringer, Leo Arms) and three Utopias to finish. All its cards exist in print.

yuma-pre-wdc-first-syllable.name: First Syllable (Gagaga)
yuma-pre-wdc-first-syllable.blurb: Yuma's deck at the start of the series: Level 4 monsters named after syllables (Gagaga, Gogogo, Dododo, Zubaba) and Number 39: Utopia as the finishing card. Joe the Pixie and anime-only cards are replaced with printed equivalents.

yuma-v-jump-gogogo-great-cannon.name: Gogogo Great Cannon
yuma-v-jump-gogogo-great-cannon.blurb: The V Jump deck (December 2013) centered on the Gogogo: Giant, Golem, Ghost and Goblindbergh to climb to Utopia, Utopia Ray V and Utopia Ray Victory. All its cards exist in print.

yuma-wdc-finals-xyz-otk.name: One-Turn Xyz
yuma-wdc-finals-xyz-otk.blurb: The Carnival finals version: many different Xyz (Utopia Ray, Leviathan Dragon, Shark Drake, ZW - Leo Arms) to close the duel in one turn. Anime-only Xyz support cards are swapped for printed Xyz support.

celina-fusion-dimension-lunalight.name: Lunalight
celina-fusion-dimension-lunalight.blurb: Celina's (Selena) deck: Lunalight, moon animals that fuse into the Dancers with Polymerization, with Lunalight Cat Dancer at the head. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Lunalights.

declan-standard-dimension-ddd.name: D/D/D
declan-standard-dimension-ddd.blurb: Declan Akaba's (Reiji) deck: D/D/D with their Dark Contracts, Pendulum Savants and kings that are Summoned by Fusion, Synchro and Xyz. One Extra Deck card is removed from the wiki list because of the 15-card limit, and anime-only cards are swapped for printed D/D/D.

dennis-standard-dimension-performage.name: Performage
dennis-standard-dimension-performage.blurb: Dennis McField's deck: Performage, artists that move around the field, with their Pendulums and the Xyz Performage Shadow Maker and Trapeze Magician. Anime-only cards are left out.

gong-standard-dimension-superheavy-samur.name: Superheavy Samurai
gong-standard-dimension-superheavy-samur.blurb: Gong Strong's (Gongenzaka) deck: defensive Superheavy Samurai that lock into defense and climb to the huge Synchros. Cards that only exist in the anime are swapped for printed Superheavy Samurai.

shay-xyz-dimension-raidraptor.name: Raidraptor
shay-xyz-dimension-raidraptor.blurb: Shay Obsidian's (Shun Kurosaki) deck: Raidraptors that overlay on each other and climb in rank with the Rank-Up-Magic Force up to Raidraptor - Ultimate Falcon. Anime-only traps and spells are swapped for printed Raidraptors.

sora-fusion-dimension-fluffal-frightfur.name: Fluffal and Frightfur
sora-fusion-dimension-fluffal-frightfur.blurb: Sora Perse's deck: Fluffal plushies and Edge Imp tools that fuse into Frightfurs like Frightfur Leo or Frightfur Sabre-Tooth. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Fluffal and Toy cards.

yugo-synchro-dimension-speedroid.name: Speedroid and Clear Wing
yugo-synchro-dimension-speedroid.blurb: Yugo's deck in the Synchro Dimension: Speedroids that Summon in a chain and Synchro up to Clear Wing Synchro Dragon and Crystal Wing Synchro Dragon. Anime-only Speed cards are replaced with printed Speedroids.

yuri-fusion-dimension-ancient-gear.name: Honor Student: Ancient Gear
yuri-fusion-dimension-ancient-gear.blurb: The honor student deck with which Yuri poses as a Duel Academy student: Ancient Gear with Polymerization to reach Ultimate Ancient Gear Golem.

yuri-fusion-dimension-predaplant.name: Predaplant
yuri-fusion-dimension-predaplant.blurb: Yuri's deck: Predaplants that put Predator Counters on the opponent's monsters and fuse them into Starving Venom Fusion Dragon. Anime-only cards are replaced with printed Predaplants.

yuto-xyz-dimension-phantom-knights.name: Phantom Knights
yuto-xyz-dimension-phantom-knights.blurb: Yuto's deck, from the Xyz Dimension: the Phantom Knights Summon themselves when their traps are activated and overlay into Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon and Dark Requiem Xyz Dragon. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Phantom Knights.

yuya-duel-academy-odd-eyes-dimensions.name: Odd-Eyes of the Four Dimensions
yuya-duel-academy-odd-eyes-dimensions.blurb: Yuya's deck at Duel Academy, now with all the Odd-Eyes: Venom (Fusion), Wing (Synchro) and Raging (Xyz) alongside Performapal. What only exists in the anime is left out or swapped for printed cards.

yuya-friendship-cup-performapal-rebellio.name: Performapal and Odd-Eyes Rebellion
yuya-friendship-cup-performapal-rebellio.blurb: Yuya's deck in the Friendship Cup: more Performapal Pendulum, the Xiangke and Xiangsheng Magicians, and the jump to Odd-Eyes Rebellion Dragon and Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Performapal and Pendulum Magician cards.

yuya-pre-arc-league-performapal.name: Performapal Odd-Eyes
yuya-pre-arc-league-performapal.blurb: The deck with which Yuya starts the series: Performapal that animate each other and Odd-Eyes Pendulum Dragon with the Magicians' Scales. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Performapal and Pendulum Magician cards.

zuzu-standard-dimension-melodious.name: Melodious
zuzu-standard-dimension-melodious.blurb: Zuzu's deck: Melodious Divas that come together with Polymerization into Bloom Diva the Melodious Choir and Bloom Prima. Anime-only cards are swapped for printed Melodious.

ai-season1-ignister.name: @Ignister
ai-season1-ignister.blurb: Ai's deck: the @Ignisters, Cyberse monsters that link up to The Arrival Cyberse @Ignister, with the anime's A.I. cards. Those that do not exist are swapped for printed @Ignisters.

george-gore-season1-gouki.name: Gouki (Celebrity Duelist)
george-gore-season1-gouki.blurb: Gore's deck as a famous duelist: Gouki fighters that link into Ogres with the Re-Match effect. The Gouki copies go up to three, as in a real list, and it is completed with staples.

george-gore-season2-dinowrestler.name: Dinowrestler (Bounty Hunter)
george-gore-season2-dinowrestler.blurb: Gore's deck as a bounty hunter: Dinowrestler with World Dino Wrestling, Tyrant Dino Fusion and Spacetime Transcendence. The anime Dinosaurs that do not exist are replaced with those from real Dinosaur lists.

skye-zaizen-season1-trickstar.name: Trickstar
skye-zaizen-season1-trickstar.blurb: Blue Angel's deck in the first season: Trickstars that inflict damage to the player when effects are activated and Trickstar Light Stage as support. It is completed with the printed Trickstars a real list plays.

skye-zaizen-season2-marincess.name: Marincess
skye-zaizen-season2-marincess.blurb: Blue Angel's aquatic deck: Marincess that link toward Marincess Coral Anemone and Great Bubble Reef. It is completed with staples from real Aqua monster lists.

spectre-season1-sunavalon.name: Sunavalon
spectre-season1-sunavalon.blurb: Spectre's deck: Sunseed and Sunvine that link into the Sunavalon and recover Sunseed Genius Loci. The copies of the base go up and it is completed with Plant support from real lists.

theodore-hamilton-season2-salamangreat.name: Salamangreat
theodore-hamilton-season2-salamangreat.blurb: Soulburner's deck: Salamangreat that revive when you Link Summon one with the same name, with Heatleo, Sunlight Wolf and Pyro Phoenix to finish. Anime-only cards are replaced with printed Salamangreat.

varis-season1-rokket-borrel.name: Rokket and Borrel (Topologic)
varis-season1-rokket-borrel.blurb: Revolver's deck in his first duel with Playmaker: Rokket dragons that send themselves to the Graveyard to reach Borrelsword, Borreload and the Topologics. Anime cards with no print are replaced with real Rokket and Borrel cards.

varis-season2-borreload-savage.name: Rokket and Borreload Savage
varis-season2-borreload-savage.blurb: Revolver's deck in the second season: the full Rokket line in three copies to reach Borreload Savage Dragon, Borreload eXcharge and Dillingerous Dragon. The Rokket copies go up to what a real list uses.

varis-season3-borreload-furious.name: Rokket and Borreload Furious
varis-season3-borreload-furious.blurb: Revolver's deck at the end of the series: Rokket with Borreload Furious Dragon, Quadborrel Dragon and Topologic Zeroboros in the Extra Deck. The Rokket base is reinforced with copies a real list plays.

yusaku-fujiki-season1-cyberse-link.name: Cyberse Link (Talkers)
yusaku-fujiki-season1-cyberse-link.blurb: Playmaker's first Cyberse deck: Link 1 and 2 to reach Decode Talker, Encode Talker and Excode Talker. Seven Links are removed from the Extra Deck to respect the 15-card limit.

yusaku-fujiki-season2-firewall-dragon.name: Firewall Dragon and Code Talker
yusaku-fujiki-season2-firewall-dragon.blurb: Playmaker's deck with Cynet Fusion, Cynet Ritual and the Firewall Dragon line: Code Talker, Transcode Talker and Firewall Dragon Darkfluid. Twelve Links are cut from the Extra Deck.

yusaku-fujiki-season3-accesscode-talker.name: Accesscode Talker and Parallel eXceed
yusaku-fujiki-season3-accesscode-talker.blurb: The third-season deck: Parallel eXceed, Cyberse Clock Dragon and Accesscode Talker to close. Cards that only exist in the anime are completed with Cyberse staples from real lists.
